Definition: Does the government maintain a separate cadastral register?
Comments: Separate GIS cadastral system via WebGIS and ArcGIS layer.
revision_notes: Original score (4, Partially deployed) rests on the cited WebGIS source, which was verified live: the Ministry of Habitat, Infrastructure and Land Transport's WebGIS Cadastre and Planning module has been operational since November 2013, offering public search of land parcels and beacons, planning-application layers and map export tools. The cited ArcGIS item page (arcgis.com id=f824e...) returned no retrievable content on fetch and could not be independently confirmed. A further search found the Lands Department/DICT tendering a new Land Management Administration Information System (LMAIS) in November 2024 and continuing to recruit GIS/survey staff (2025) to maintain the national survey control network and cadastral layers, indicating an established but still-evolving digital cadastral function. Score of 4 confirmed; not upgraded to 5 because the WebGIS itself is explicitly non-live/for-information-only and the authoritative cadastral system is still being modernised.
revised_comments: Seychelles maintains a separate digital cadastral register through the Ministry of Habitat, Infrastructure and Land Transport's WebGIS platform, operational since November 2013, which gives the public search access to land parcels and survey beacons for Mahé and the other islands, together with cadastral and planning layers, in line with the Cadastral Survey Act. The WebGIS notes that its data is compiled periodically rather than live, with authoritative cadastral survey records maintained separately by the Lands Department's Survey Division, which continues to invest in digitisation of the national survey control network and cadastral mapping. This constitutes a partially deployed digital cadastral system rather than a fully integrated real-time one.

Definition: Does the government maintain a digital land register?
Comments: Land Registry under Registration Division. Online land search request form, WebGIS for cadastral, ArcGIS cadastral layer updated 2023. Partially deployed.
revision_notes: Original score (4, Partially deployed) cited a static 'Land Search Request Form' publication describing a manual, email-based search request process, and two cadastral (not title-register) sources, which only weakly support the land-register score. Verified instead via the Seychelles Registration Division website and its Land Registry eSearch portal (registry.gov.sc/LandRegistry), which confirm an electronic search system covering title deeds, charges, transfers and discharges exists, though subscription still requires an in-person visit to the Office of the Registrar General. Further search found the Lands Department, with DICT, tendering a new Land Management Administration Information System (LMAIS) in November 2024 (interfacing with SeyID, the National Population Database, Immigration and IFMIS) and a related Land Valuation System in 2025, showing the comprehensive digital land register/management system is still under active development. Score of 4 confirmed rather than upgraded, since core registration remains substantially manual pending LMAIS rollout.
revised_comments: Seychelles maintains a digital land register administered by the Registration Division, which operates a Land Registry eSearch electronic search platform covering title deeds, charges, transfers, leases and discharges for Old and New Land Registries, alongside its physical archives. Access to eSearch requires in-person subscription at the Office of the Registrar General rather than online self-registration, and land registration transactions themselves remain a substantially manual, in-office process. The Lands Department, working with the Department of Information Communications Technology, is developing a new Land Management Administration Information System to modernise land administration and interface it with the national population database, digital identity system, immigration records and public financial management system, alongside a companion Land Valuation System tendered in 2025. This reflects a partially deployed digital land register that is in the process of being substantially upgraded.
